datasets.title: Research publications by institution
datasets.description: Annual OpenAlex work counts for eight selected institutional comparators.
notes: Institution-affiliated works cover all research fields, not health research alone. They are not NHHR-attributable outputs.
Institution counts overlap when a work has multiple affiliations; do not sum them into a regional total.
Coverage reflects the collected OpenAlex snapshot; 2025 may have indexing lag. Absolute workstation source paths are excluded.

datasets.title: CIHR annual payments
datasets.description: Fiscal-year payments recorded for selected institutions, with incomplete 2025 payment coverage removed.
notes: Fiscal-year payments are not lifetime award commitments. This release omits total_awarded to prevent adding commitments repeatedly across fiscal years.
FY 2025 has project records but amount_paid_fy is zero for every comparator in the source. Payment coverage is incomplete; these rows are excluded, not interpreted as zero funding.
Comparator totals reflect NHHR institution matching and collected coverage; no per-capita or NHHR-attributable value is inferred.

datasets.title: NSERC awards by institution
datasets.description: Award amounts and award counts for selected institutional comparators by fiscal year.
notes: NSERC supports natural sciences and engineering; these figures are a broad research-capacity comparator, not health funding alone.
Award amounts are the source measure and are not directly interchangeable with CIHR annual payments.
Distinct awards and source rows differ for some institutions; preserve this distinction when comparing counts.

datasets.title: Clinical trials with an exact-city site
datasets.description: ClinicalTrials.gov site matches in seven comparator cities, retained as city counts.
notes: Exact city-string matches identify registered study sites, not local enrollments, accessible trials, or a health-authority catchment.
Counts include historical statuses. Recruiting fields describe the collected snapshot and are not live recruitment advice.
A multi-site study can appear in more than one city. City boundaries and HSDA/LHA boundaries are different geographies; no polygon join or rate is inferred.

datasets.title: Prince George registered study portfolio
datasets.description: Ten exact-site registry studies with coded condition and intervention domains.
notes: Public registry identifiers and facilities are retained; personal contact names, emails, phones, and interview targets are excluded.
A study listing does not establish local enrollment, screening capacity, participant eligibility, or current recruitment. Follow the registry link for current details.
NHHR domain coding is an analytical interpretation. Registry completion dates may be planned dates.

datasets.title: Physician supply across BC health regions

datasets.sourceName: CIHI public physician statistics · NHHR regional summary
notes: Counts are the collected public regional physician measure, not vacancies, full-time equivalents, local appointment access, or NHHR research staff.
Rates are preserved from the reviewed source; no rates are recomputed using the suspect population summaries.
Source 59xx health-region codes join to the corresponding two-digit BC HSDA codes using an explicit crosswalk. Boundaries show regions, not physician locations.

datasets.title: Northern local health area populations
datasets.description: BC Stats total population rows for seventeen Northern local health areas, with projections labelled.

LHA population is a regional denominator, not a city population or a count of patients served. Boundary codes refer to the source LHA geography.

datasets.title: Travel cost assumptions and benchmarks
datasets.description: Five collected mileage, fare, and economic-cost benchmarks with distinct units and evidence limits.
datasets.sourceName: CRA / NH Connections · NHHR collected benchmarks
notes: Values have different units; never add or rank them as a common cost. Select one benchmark and read its unit and evidence note.
The $20 fare record is described as news-sourced in the collected table and lacks its original news citation. It requires verification before use.
Economic driving cost is a derived mileage scenario, not an observed patient expense. CRA allowances are tax benchmarks, not measured medical-travel costs.

datasets.title: Hypothetical avoided-travel scenarios
datasets.description: Three planning cases showing the effect of assumed reach, avoided trips, trip cost, and patient time.
notes: These are hypothetical inputs and calculations, not measured NHHR benefits, forecasts, avoided trips, or causal effects.
Travel value = avoided trips × cost per trip. Patient time value = patients reached × hours saved per patient × value per hour.
The original scenario table carries the doubled Northern population denominator (596414). That field is omitted; no population-based uptake or rate is shown.

datasets.title: Validation questions still open
datasets.description: Thirteen institution-level requests that describe evidence still needed for feasibility decisions.
notes: This is a request tracker, not supplied enrollment, staffing, financial, governance, or interview evidence. One row represents one evidence request.
No completed interview findings are included in this snapshot. Interview guides, recruitment materials, or blank coding workbooks must not be presented as interview results.
Personal contacts, interview candidates, consent records, participant-level data, and internal remuneration are excluded. Community governance acceptability cannot be inferred from public sources.

stories.title: Where specialist supply is thinnest
stories.summary: Compare Northern health regions with the rest of BC, using the source’s 2024 physician rates.
body: The Northern profile spans Northwest, Northern Interior, and Northeast health service delivery areas. The map joins public regional counts and rates to their corresponding HSDA boundaries.
In the collected 2024 source, Northern specialist rates range from 26.5 to 95.9 per 100,000 people. Explore each region rather than treating Northern BC as one uniform workforce.
Physician supply helps frame feasibility questions. It does not measure vacancies, appointment waits, research coordinator capacity, or the impact of NHHR. Those require validation evidence.

stories.title: A small registered portfolio, a concrete starting point
stories.summary: The collected registry snapshot contains 10 studies with a Prince George site. What could expand local trial access?
body: Prince George has 10 exact-city study matches in the collected summary, including 7 coded oncology studies. Open the study portfolio to inspect titles, facilities, domains, and public registry links.
City-site counts establish a recorded footprint. They do not show local enrollment, protocol eligibility, screening failures, operating capacity, or whether a listed trial is available now.

Use the evidence tracker to identify the next questions for institutions: enrollment and referral pathways, staffing, governance requirements, and community priorities. Interview findings are not included in this public snapshot.

stories.title: Research capacity in context
stories.summary: Read publications, CIHR payments, and NSERC awards as complementary evidence of institutional scale.
body: The collected OpenAlex table records 523 UNBC-affiliated works in 2025. Compare the five-year series with selected institutions, keeping institutional scope and overlapping affiliations in view.

CIHR payments describe recorded fiscal-year cash flow, while NSERC amounts describe the source award measure. Different measures and broad institutional mandates make a single combined league table misleading.

CIHR 2025 project records all carry zero payments in this collected summary. The explorer excludes that year from the paid series because payment coverage is incomplete. Public funding and publications do not establish NHHR-attributable returns.

stories.title: Count people once before calculating a rate
stories.summary: A verified source-row check corrects a doubled Northern population denominator and enables LHA mapping.
body: The collected health-authority summary reports Northern at 596,414 in 2025. Tracing it to the original BC Stats rows shows Female + Male + Total were added together. The Gender=T source total is 298,207.

The same duplication appears in the selected LHA summary. Prince George LHA is 105,544 in the raw total row, compared with 211,088 in the earlier summary. The atlas uses one total row per LHA and year.
Explore the Northern LHA map with the source estimate/projection type visible. These are health-area populations, not municipal populations or NHHR participants, and 2025 is a projection.

stories.title: What would reducing travel be worth?
stories.summary: Explore three planning cases and the assumptions that drive modelled travel and patient time values.
body: The base case assumes 300 patients reached, 450 avoided trips, and $900 per trip, producing $405,000 in modelled travel value. Its patient-time calculation assumes six hours per person at $35 per hour, producing $63,000.

These calculations illustrate how assumptions affect potential value. They are not observed benefits, forecasts, or evidence that NHHR has avoided any trips. The doubled population field in the original scenario source is omitted.

Read the collected route patterns and benchmark evidence notes alongside the scenarios. Historical schedules, subsidized fares, economic mileage costs, and patient out-of-pocket expenses represent different questions.

stories.title: From public evidence to a validated operating model
stories.summary: The evidence tracker makes missing information visible instead of filling gaps with assumed results.
body: Thirteen institution-level requests describe the information still needed to test feasibility: trial enrollment, staffing, space, funding pathways, travel burden, and governance expectations.
Public registry, publication, funding, and workforce datasets can help choose questions. They cannot establish community permission, operational readiness, causal effects, or partner commitments.
No completed interview findings appear in this released snapshot. Recruitment scripts, consent templates, or blank analysis workbooks are preparation materials and should not be treated as findings.

snapshot.releaseScope: Bounded public-secondary aggregates and public registry records; explicit planning scenarios and review findings.
limitations: Collected source snapshots are historical, not live data.
Interview, consent, contact, remuneration, and participant records are excluded.
Source privacy classification is not blanket release permission; only explicitly allowlisted columns are included.
